headline: Former president's ex-wife Bidisha Siddique arrested in fraud case
summary: Police arrested the former spouse of Hussain Muhammad Ershad in Gulshan, Dhaka, in connection with a 2008 fraud case.
details: Police have arrested Bidisha Siddique, the former wife of former President Hussain Muhammad Ershad, from the Gulshan area of Dhaka.
The arrest is linked to a fraud case filed in 2008.
Bidisha Siddique was previously married to the former president, and the arrest follows long-standing legal proceedings regarding the fraud allegations.
She has been taken into custody by law enforcement agencies for further investigation and legal action.

headline_marked: Poultry farmers [[block highway in Gazipur]] over feed price hikes
headline: Poultry farmers block highway in Gazipur over feed price hikes
summary: Marginal farmers protested against the abnormal increase in poultry feed prices, disrupting traffic on the Dhaka-Mymensingh highway.
details: Marginal poultry farmers in Gazipur staged a protest and blocked the Dhaka-Mymensingh highway at the Jaina Bazar area on August 25.
The farmers are protesting against the abnormal increase in the price of poultry feed, which has made it difficult for them to maintain their farms.
The blockade disrupted traffic on one of the country's major highways, causing significant delays for commuters and vehicles.
The protesters demanded a reduction in feed prices to ensure the survival of their livelihoods as marginal farmers.
caption:
Poultry farmers in Gazipur have blocked a major highway to protest skyrocketing feed prices.

Marginal poultry farmers in Gazipur staged a protest and blocked the Dhaka-Mymensingh highway at the Jaina Bazar area on August 25.

The farmers are protesting against the abnormal increase in the price of poultry feed, which has made it difficult for them to maintain their farms.

The blockade disrupted traffic on one of the country's major highways, causing significant delays for commuters and vehicles.

The protesters demanded a reduction in feed prices to ensure the survival of their livelihoods as marginal farmers.
